description: otoole is a Python package for handling inputs and results for OSeMOSYS energy-system optimization models. It converts among supported input formats, checks and visualizes data, and processes result files from multiple solvers. A model’s geography, technology set and planning horizon come from the supplied OSeMOSYS files; otoole is not a fixed energy dataset. Its public repository and documentation are MIT licensed. The tool can help build reproducible electricity, heat or fuel pathway scenarios and compare capacity-expansion outputs across workflows. A caveat is that format conversion cannot establish whether demand, technology costs or solver settings are correct, and a user still needs an OSeMOSYS model and appropriate solver. The catalogue model-osemosys describes the optimization engine, while this is a distinct data interface. No first-review draft or catalogue software record matched otoole. This review read the JOSS summary, own repository and README, but did not convert files or solve a model. Geographic coverage follows the supplied OSeMOSYS scenario.
